_doc: Neutral back-end defaults (opentool). Lengths in mm on the print. Merge order: these <- printer profile <- style profile <- game profile 'backend' <- class <- weapons <- unit files <- job overrides. Taste rules (eye-height targets, base style) live in style profiles, game facts in game profiles.

adaptive_voxel._doc: Memory-safe solid stage: the voxel is chosen so the predicted build peak stays inside the runner cap (runner.mem_gb). Predicted peak_gb = fixed_gb + gb_per_mtri x remeshed Mtris, remeshed Mtris = ref_mtris x surface/ref_area x (ref_voxel/voxel)^2. Calibrated 2026-11-07 on the v1 Intercessor (surface 5806 mm2, 18.65 Mtris at 0.03 mm): at 0.05 mm the build part peaked at 14.9 GB committed and the separate final remesh at 11.3 GB. A voxel is only ever made coarser than geometry.voxel_mm. If a build still hits the cap, the build stage retries once with voxel_retry_factor x the voxel (logged in the report).

geometry._doc_remesh_process: 'separate': the final voxel remesh, cleanup, decimate and export run in their own Blender process from a saved union mesh, so the probes and the subdivided copies are gone from memory (under the 16 GB cap). 'same': v1 behaviour, one process.

connect_floating._doc_axis: elongated floating parts (antenna tips, rods, spikes) left unbridged get a connector continuing their own axis to the nearest real surface within max_axis_gap_mm
connect_floating._doc_v1: axis_bridge / thin_wall_fallback / eroded_volume_factor < 1 are off here so the v1 Intercessor regression reproduces; the big classes turn them on

loose_items._doc: Props held in a hand that are not the weapon (grenades...) move to the belt: mirrored from a matching item already on the pelvis, else offset to the hip. Patterns come from the game profile.

pose_select._doc: Pick visually distinct, printable frames from the unit's own clips. Clip roles come from the adapter (idle/aim/shoot/move/melee/die/other).

flag._doc: check stage: a job that still fails these after the build's own repairs is FLAGGED (never silently fixed).
flag._doc_thin: thin parts (walls under qa.min_thickness) are flagged when they reach at least thin_part_min_protrusion_mm beyond thick material (spike tips, antennae); shorter lips are displacement fringes on plate rims that the 0.2 mm nozzle merges

scale._doc: rule: eye_height (sole contact plane to pupil line = eye_height_mm), metric (real metres x mm_per_metre, from the package's metres_per_unit), factor (mm per imported unit, fixed). 'auto' = eye_height for infantry, metric for the rest. eye: where the pupil line comes from - the rig's eye role, else a fraction of the head mesh height (flagged as estimated on the sheet), or eye_line_raw given per unit.

flying_large.note: GW 'Large Flying Base' (60 mm flying base + stem): socket for the stem; diameter to be confirmed by test-fitting (stem_socket_gauge.stl)

flying_small.note: GW 'Small Flying Base' (32 mm flying base + short stem): the print gets a socket for the stem; socket diameter to be confirmed by test-fitting a real stem (pipeline/output/_gauges/stem_socket_gauge.stl)

hull.note: GW: no base, the model stands on its hull/tracks

unique.note: GW: model fits no standard base (agree with the event organiser); built without a base, flagged

32mm.note: Citadel 32 mm round: 32.0 bottom, 30.0 top, 4.0 tall, straight taper (confirmed)

base_finish._doc: neutral: plain flat top with sole prisms closing tiny gaps under the feet. Style/game profiles add terrain or a dome.

review._doc: review sheet: numbered views at one scale, silhouette, close-ups of hands / feet / weapon

contact._doc: checks: parts 0-0.5 mm apart are a contact band, bridged in print prep (listed, not an error); a boot more than band_mm off the base fails
